The module carries only the surface the two CLI modules use and is pinned by ten target-only cases, because it is new code with no source to underwrite it (rule 11).

target_only_tests.why: Ten, all of them about `src/cli/parser.ts` and `src/cli.ts` -- code this port had to write because Node has no argparse, and which therefore carries no warrant from interlock (rule 11). Two of the ten exist because a mutation sweep found the ported cases could not see the property they name: `the help walk reaches the mounted subcommand's own flags` closes the hazard that both cp932 cases are a loop over helpStrings and a walk returning nothing makes both vacuously green, and `half a corpus reference is refused for being half` closes an inherited blind spot -- the ported case (and its source) point --fixture-corpus at a directory that does not exist, so loadCorpus refuses with a FixtureRefusal, which IS a ControlPlaneRefusal, and the case stays green with the half-reference guard deleted (measured). The remaining eight pin the parser's own refusals: a required flag, a value outside a flag's choices, a flag given twice, three spellings of a non-integer millisecond value, --help routed to the subcommand rather than the root, and the version flag.

test/measurement/cli.test.ts::read-only by capability > the command opens no writable connection
entries.reason: The source records every `sqlite3.connect` the process makes and asserts each was a `file:...?mode=ro` URI opened with `uri=True`. better-sqlite3 accepts no URI filename, so continuo's first read-only mechanism is the driver's `readonly: true` open flag (D-0100), and the assertion is `readonly: true` on every open. The interception moves too: ESM bindings cannot be rebound from outside, so `vi.mock` replaces the driver MODULE for every importer, which preserves the property the source case is built on -- a writable handle opened by anyone under the command fails it. Measured: with openReadOnlyImpl lowered to `readonly: false`, this case goes red.

entries.target_id: test/measurement/cli.test.ts::read-only by capability > the command module imports no other opener
entries.reason: The source asks the imported module object two questions -- `not hasattr(measurement_cli, 'sqlite3')` and `open_for_measurement.__module__` -- and an ES module object answers neither: it exposes only what it exports, and an import is not a property of it. The same two questions are put to the module's TEXT, which is where an import lives in this language: the import list must contain `./reader.js` and no opener, and the file must contain no `new Database`. Measured: with openDatabase imported into cli.ts, this case goes red.

test/measurement/cli.test.ts::cp932 > every help string is ASCII
entries.reason: D-0113. Node has no cp932 encoder, so `text.encode('cp932')` has no counterpart. The source asserts BOTH `encode('cp932')` and `text.isascii()`; ASCII is a subset of cp932, so the port asserts the second and it implies the first. The walk itself is ported to helpStrings in src/cli/parser.ts, and a target-only case pins that the walk reaches the innermost parser -- without it this loop is vacuously green.

entries.target_id: test/measurement/cli.test.ts::cp932 > the help of the mounted subcommand is ASCII
entries.reason: D-0113, as above. Here the port asserts STRICTLY MORE than its source, which checks only cp932-encodability for the filtered strings and not isascii(): there is no weaker check available in this runtime. Recorded as adapted rather than passing silently, because rule 0 makes a stronger assertion in a ported slot a divergence like any other. The source's filter (`measure` / `measurement` / `fingerprint` in the text) is carried across unchanged.

entries.target_id: test/measurement/cli.test.ts::cp932 > help runs in a real console and writes only ASCII bytes
entries.reason: D-0113. The source sets PYTHONIOENCODING=cp932 so the child's stdout raises on a character it cannot encode; Node writes UTF-8 whatever the console is, so there is no stream encoding to set and no exception to provoke. The port checks the bytes that actually left the process instead -- `--help` must write only bytes below 0x80, which are the same bytes in cp932 -- and keeps the source's other two assertions (exit 0, `--fingerprint` present) unchanged. It drives the BUILT dist/cli.js, which is why the case asserts that file exists first: section 10 instance 1 is the same subprocess-without-a-build hazard.

mutation_sweep.ran: 23 mutations, one per property the cases in this file claim to pin, across src/measurement/cli.ts, src/cli/parser.ts, src/cli.ts and the one line of src/measurement/reader.ts the read-only claim rests on. Harness kept at .sweep/ and not committed.
mutation_sweep.note: The FIRST run of this sweep reported 21 of 21 caught, and eight of those verdicts were worthless: six mutations were `if (false)`, which TypeScript refuses, so the build failed and the harness read a failed run as a caught mutation, and two more had their JSON report mis-sliced because vitest prints its pretty failure output to the same stream. That is section 10's own hazard -- red for a reason other than the one being tested -- reached from inside the tool built to check for it. The harness now reports INCONCLUSIVE for a build that refuses a mutation and writes its report to a file rather than to stdout, and every always-false condition is written to survive the type-checker.

closed_survivors.mutation: an integer flag keeps only the safe-integer half of its guard
closed_survivors.verdict: the target-only case could not distinguish the two guards, widened
closed_survivors.note: `--period-start-ms 1.5` is refused by Number.isSafeInteger alone, and the case matched a message prefix both guards share. Widened to 0x10 (Number gives 16) and the empty string (Number gives 0 -- a period boundary quietly at the epoch), and the assertion now matches the whole message. Whitespace padding is deliberately NOT refused: `int(' 12 ')` is 12 in Python, so refusing it would make the port stricter than what it is a port of.

divergences.behaviour: The CLI is parsed by a purpose-built parser rather than by argparse, and it accepts less than argparse does: long flags only, one value each, no positional arguments, no prefix matching, no nargs. It also refuses two command lines argparse accepts -- a flag given twice (argparse keeps the last) and an integer spelled `0x10` or `` (Python's int() refuses both, so this half is parity, not divergence).

The two cp932 help-string cases assert ASCII rather than cp932-encodability, and the subprocess case checks the bytes `--help` wrote rather than setting the child's stdout encoding. Node has neither a cp932 encoder nor a PYTHONIOENCODING equivalent.
`the command opens no writable connection` asserts the driver's readonly open flag rather than a `mode=ro` URI. Recorded here because this case is the one that asserts it on the whole call path.
The top-level CLI mounts one subtree where interlock's mounts six; the other five name modules continuo has not ported.
